verdicts.why: Reads formality and propriety of manner as the word's content and keeps the coolness descriptive rather than approving, matching the neutral charge.
Formal-or-perfunctory politeness is exactly what the note describes, the neutral charge fits the 'perfunctory' branch, and both Austen examples show that cool form.
Treats the bare gloss 'a courteous manner' as the unmarked base and differentiates by what neighbours add, staying inside the word.
Courteous regard for feelings with a yielding in it fits the gloss and the example 'in deference to your wishes'.
Marks the object (women) that the gloss itself names and contrasts it with plain courtesy; charge positive is plausible.
Excellence rather than mere adequacy of manners is the gloss, and the ranking against civility is a word-to-word contrast.
Describes courteous conduct respecting accepted usage with mild approval; 'plainest name' is a register observation, not a frequency claim.
Aims the courtesy at another's feelings, as the gloss says, and the example 'out of respect for his privacy' is this sense.
Over-eager speed with carelessness close behind is the gloss; register comparison with hurry stays inside the word and examples fit.
Keeps the carelessness as 'possible', as the gloss does, and the letter example shows regretted over-eager speed.
The bare rate with no reproach fits the neutral gloss and the 'gratifying speed' example.
Same rate read as an admired quality is a plausible force for the word and justifies the positive charge against speed's neutral.
Admirable quality framed as credit weighable against fault fits the gloss, and all three examples are this sense.
Puts the 'high' of the gloss into the word and contrasts with worth; 'far above rubies' is exactly this sense.
Unsigned positive-or-negative appraisal is what the gloss says, the neutral charge matches, and 'dubious value' fits.
Attribute presented as already admirable fits the gloss and the contrast with value's weighing stays inside the words.
Covers desirable, valuable or useful as the gloss lists them and distinguishes from price's built-in height.
Moral wrongness covering both principle and practice tracks the gloss exactly; examples fit.
Something that holds you back read as a practical drag, not a moral verdict, fits the gloss and negative charge.
Locates the quality in the embarrassment of a situation as the gloss does; the proposal example fits.
Failing as something missing or broken inside the thing fits 'a failing or deficiency', and the examples are this sense.
Plain statement of an inferior or less favourable position, without accusation, fits the gloss and a mild negative charge.
Hindrance in the way of getting on is the gloss, and the contrast with defect's emptiness is word-to-word.
Competitive standing below rivals is exactly the gloss; the contrast with disadvantage stays inside the words.
Boundary with no failing charged fits 'limited or restricted' and supports the neutral charge.
Painful consequence earned by an action or condition is the gloss, and 'paid the penalty' fits.
Failing as falling short of a mark fits the gloss and differentiates from defect without leaving the word.
Poor-example sense is honoured, the negative charge fits, and both 'apology for a meal/dinner' examples are this idiom; the rueful-versus-blunt contrast with excuse is a defensible reading of force.
